pages.title: Haber-Bosch Reactor
pages.text: Hydrogen and nitrogen pressed together over hot iron: the reaction that fixes the air's nitrogen into ammonia, and feeds half the world.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry - and JEI - show the pattern.

Set the temperature, the pressure and the hydrogen-to-nitrogen ratio. The equilibrium (van 't Hoff, from ΔG° = ΔH − TΔS) favours ammonia when cold and pressed; the iron only works fast when hot. A pass needs at least 15% ammonia. The iron sinters above 823 K (it then wears ten times as fast); the vessel is rated to 300 atm. Needs an Iron Catalyst in its catalyst slot.
